Miche Baker's Percentage

One very large round, often from a kilo of flour, that needs a wide basket and a slow rise so it does not spill over.

Detailed method

One large round from a kilo of flour. Currently 1000 g flour, 78% hydration, 15% starter, 2% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 780 g water, 150 g starter, 20 g salt, and 0 g yeast, 1950 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 79.5% effective hydration. Currently 1 loaf of 1950 g. The lower starter gives this much dough time to rise. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 150 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total. The yeast amount is 0 g.
  2. Mix Stir 1000 g flour, 780 g water, the 150 g starter, 0 g instant yeast, and 20 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 78% the dough is soft and heavy. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 4 to 5 hours. Fold it three times in the first 2 hours. With 15% starter it is ready when it has grown by about half, not when the bowl is full.
  4. Shape Tighten the 1950 g into one round and set it seam-side up in a wide floured basket. This batch is 1 loaf. The default 1950 g uses a round lidded pot about 28 cm across and 12 cm high. If you change the amount, use a larger pot in proportion or split the dough into two loaves.
  5. Proof Cover it for 60 to 90 minutes, until it looks puffy. A large loaf with 15% starter needs this extra time. Bake it if the top starts to sink.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with the lidded pot. Score a cross. Bake 25 minutes covered, then 25 to 35 minutes uncovered, until the crust is deep brown and the loaf sounds hollow. If you have no lid, invert another pot or a deep tray over it for the first 25 minutes. Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours before you slice.
